applies_why: The judge text decides whether Acts 2:30 and the loins/seed row count by treating the responses as answering them and the result as underdetermined, so it is within the rule governing unanswered-witness counting.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: counts as an unanswered witness -- I weighed whether the judge must quote a pressed sentence only when it actually counts a verse as unanswered, versus whenever it mentions the verse in an underdetermined ruling; I read the rule as triggered by counting as unanswered.
why: Because the judge states the row was answered and leaves the chains underdetermined, it does not count the verse as an unanswered witness or toward a broken link.
